locator.section: 8.9 Decompositions of cyclic structures (two bonds cleaved)

evidence.curator_note: Substrate is the 1,2-dimethylpiperidine molecular ion: the page prints '+.' on the ring nitrogen, so the precursor mapped_smiles localizes both the charge and the odd electron on N(1) (three sigma bonds on N+ leave one unpaired electron), exactly as drawn. Book draws 2 arc(s); moves <1,2> are drawn, move <3> is an implicit homolysis hook required for electron balance (not drawn on the page). Drawn arc 1 = a fishhook from the odd electron printed on N(1) into the N(1)-C(2) bond; drawn arc 2 = a fishhook from the C(2)-CH3(8) sigma bond into that same N(1)-C(2) bond, which therefore rises from single to double (immonium). The undrawn move 3 carries the second electron of the cleaved C(2)-CH3 bond onto C(8); the book simply writes CH3 off the page and prints the resulting (M-CH3)+ ion. Note the methyl that leaves is the RING-carbon methyl on C(2), not the N-methyl C(7), which is retained in the m/z 98 ion as drawn. Map numbers: 1 = N, 2 = C2 (alpha ring carbon), 3-6 = ring C3..C6, 7 = N-methyl (retained), 8 = C2-methyl (expelled).

locator.section: 8.9 Decompositions of cyclic structures (two bonds cleaved)

evidence.curator_note: Book draws 3 arc(s) on the m/z 98 structure; moves <1,2,3> are ALL drawn and no implicit hook is needed - this is an even-electron retro-Diels-Alder, i.e. a three-arrow cyclic two-electron flow, and every arrowhead on the page is a full (double-barbed) head, hence electron_count 2 throughout. Drawn arc 1 = the N(1)=C(2) pi pair sliding to C(2)=C(3); drawn arc 2 = the C(3)-C(4) sigma pair becoming the C(4)=C(5) pi bond of the expelled ethylene; drawn arc 3 = the C(5)-C(6) sigma pair becoming the new N(1)=C(6) pi bond. Net: the C(3)-C(4) and C(5)-C(6) ring bonds break and CH2=N+(CH3)-CH=CH2 (m/z 70) plus CH2=CH2 are formed, exactly the two structures drawn to the right. HONEST LABEL NOTE: the arrow on the page is labelled with a single italic 'i' (McLafferty's charge-site/inductive initiation), while the running text on the same page calls this an 'RDA decomposition'; step_class is set from the text (retro_diels_alder) and the printed 'i' is recorded here rather than silently dropped. The expelled CH3 radical of the first step is carried through this state as a spectator so that the step stays atom- and electron-balanced.

rule_index.json 'by_equation' has NO entry for equation 8.61 (its chapter-8 keys stop at 8.14), so no MOD rule variable is cross-linked and none is asserted. Two candidates were CHECKED rather than assumed. (i) IMS_4_43_ (DFS '[C]1([H]2)([H]3)([H]4)[C]5([H]6)([H]7)[N+.]8([H]9)[C]10([H]11)([H]12)[C]13([H]14)([H]15)[H]16>>[C]1([H]2)([H]3)([H]4)[C]5([H]6)([H]7)[N+]8([H]9){=}[C]10([H]11)([H]12).[C.]13([H]14)([H]15)[H]16') is the correct amine alpha-cleavage geometry - the cleaved C(10)-C(13) bond IS incident to the pi-forming carbon C(10) - but it does NOT match this substrate: it requires the alpha carbon to carry at least two hydrogens and a methyl beyond it on BOTH nitrogen arms, whereas the alpha carbon of 1,2-dimethylpiperidine bears only one H. Verified with RDKit: SMARTS [CH3][C;H2,H3][N+]([C;H2,H3][CH3]) gives 0 matches on the precursor. (ii) No retro-Diels-Alder rule is indexed at all: the two variables whose names end in '_rd' (IMS_4_37_rd, IMS_4_42_rd) are radical DISPLACEMENT rules that form a new C-heteroatom ring bond, not RDA ring cleavages, and the IMS_8_6_* family fragments an all-carbon open chain. So the second step of this equation has no MOD counterpart either. The page prints its abundances ('m/z 98, 100%', 'm/z 70, 12%') as bare percentages without naming the experiment; they are the book's standard 70 eV EI values (running head '8 / Detailed Mechanisms of Ion Fragmentation') and ms_context is set accordingly.
